comment: Pinned sources for the prompt-injection eval (U13 / R17). Every file is fetched at its commit into evals/injection/.cache by `npx tsx evals/injection/fetch.ts`; nothing here is redistributed except the few strings in samples.json and templates.json, each attributed in NOTICE. `role` says how the eval uses a source: dev (the rules were tuned against it), test (never looked at while tuning), held-out (local only, never vendored, never committed beyond counts).

sources.name: cyberseceval-prompt-injection
sources.licenceNote: The repository root is the Llama 3.2 Community License; the benchmark directory is MIT. Cite CybersecurityBenchmarks/LICENSE.
sources.use: The 55 rows with injection_type=indirect are positives, split by prompt_id parity: odd ids dev, even ids test. The 196 direct rows are out of scope (user-typed attacks) and are not scored.

sources.name: bipia-text-attacks
sources.licenceNote: MIT for the repository's own work, including the attack strings. The carve-out in LICENSE covers the host datasets under benchmark/ (WikiTableQuestions and Stack Exchange are CC-BY-SA-4.0); none of them is used. Repository archived 2026-09-16, hence the pinned commit.
sources.use: Attack goals, composed into synthetic product-page text by the harness. text_attack_train.json is dev, text_attack_test.json is test.

sources.name: agentdojo-attack-templates
sources.use: The five fixed wrapper strings (direct, ignore_previous, system_message, injecagent, important_instructions), copied verbatim into templates.json and wrapped around every BIPIA goal, plus the goal bare.

sources.name: wainjectbench-text
sources.licenceNote: No LICENSE file, and it aggregates CC-BY-NC material from Meta's WASP. Held out: fetched only with --held-out, read locally, never vendored, only counts and rates are committed.
sources.use: Held-out benchmark: real benign web text for the false-positive rate, and web-borne injections by subset.

notUsed.name: SEP
notUsed.reason: Optional per the addendum (CC-BY-4.0 dataset). Not needed for the first measurement; the held-out WAInjectBench benign text is the harder negative set.

notUsed.name: JailbreakBench, deepset/prompt-injections, Lakera Gandalf, HackAPrompt
notUsed.reason: Direct jailbreak corpora; the threat here is indirect injection in page text.

published.note: Meta's private direct-jailbreak benchmark and AgentDojo; not our corpus. Run on our corpus with evals/injection/promptguard.py once the gated model is accessible.
